newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House seeks more from White House on Medicare.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House seeks more from White House on Medicare.

text.p: House Budget Committee chairman John Kasich said Wednesday Republicans welcomed the administration's offer of an additional $18 billion in savings from the Medicare program, but would need greater savings still to reach agreement on changes in the program.

Office of Management and Budget director Frank Raines presented new proposals to Congress Tuesday to bring total Medicare savings up to $100 billion over five years, as calculated using more conservative congressional forecasts.

"It was a step forward for them to put an additional $18 billion in Medicare savings on the table but it isn't enough and we have asked them for four or five other things," Kasich, an Ohio Republican, told reporters after speaking to the Independent Insurance Agents.
"They should be complimented for that. That is an indication that they are serious," he added.
